newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Bonos ended dropped sharply on Tuesday after remarks by the central bank and strong US data.
Governor Luis Angel Rojo said the bank had reduced its medium term inflation target to around two percent, but he also warned that the decline in Spanish yields might be over soon.
"It's important they slashed the inflation target, but it's also important the fall in long-term yields could be close to an end," said Riccardo Barbieri, economist at Morgan Stanley.
"The bono-Bund spread is close to the key 100 basis points level and I think Rojo's comment will have just encouraged profit-taking," said Mark Geddes, economist at London research firm 4cast Ltd.
"Also we've seen some switching into Italy ahead of an expected rate cut there later this week," added Geddes. The spread between the two countries was at 65 basis points.
At the short end of the curve dealers expect tomorow's auction of six-month bills to produce a record low, with the yield seen at around 5.90 percent.
U.S. housing starts, which were stronger than expected, prompted a fall in Treasuries ahead of the Federal Reserve monetary policy meeting, which also depressed bonos, dealers said.
